scope: One existing parse_input_source mutation only; consumer/error propagation and diagnosis text contract. Not independent Spec continuation and not SK01 replacement.
proof: Mutation only affects the nonreserved <node>.<output> arm; start/resource/engine paths are byte-for-byte unchanged.
rest.empty && rest.contains(dot) is always false. The mutant consequently proceeds to NodeId::new(head) and validate_id(rest,output).

For an originally accepted value, head is a valid node ID and rest is a valid nonempty dot-free output ID. Both original and mutant run those same constructors and return exactly the same InputSource::Node.

For a newly bypassed special guard (rest empty or containing dot), either the earlier NodeId check rejects the head, or validate_id rejects the rest: empty rejected explicitly, dot rejected by allowed ASCII a-z/0-9/hyphen rule. Therefore no originally rejected value becomes accepted.

Both validation errors are mapped by the identical invalid closure to Error::FlowInvalid {rule:parse,path:the same caller path,reason:truthful explanation}. A double-invalid head/rest may change which truthful component explanation is shown, but remains the same from-field locator and error class.

Core performs no IO. parse_flow convert propagates the same from-field parse error, stopping before a usable FlowDef/compile. WorkbookRepo load_tree returns Error::Core before request/business registration; prior source staging/control objects allowed by C002 occur in the same order on both paths. No new workbook row, final business directory, request, audit or command decision is generated.

CLI keeps FLOW_INVALID, exit1, next=[], detail.rule=parse and detail.path unchanged; detail.reason and message embed changed explanation, so their bytes are explicitly NOT equal. Extra ID construction/formatting changes allocation work; no operational/business side-effect difference is claimed beyond the contract scope.

detail.path/detail.rule identify the rule; no workbook row/final directory, possible owned pending. No required literal explanation text.
Enough location fields (path/field/rule) and stable protocol error-code mapping. Both explanations retain the same field locator and truthfully name an invalid source component.
